answer: Attention-Forfeiture Windows. Each identity must hold a continuously refreshed session token whose renewal consumes 30 minutes of verified, task-relevant attention per day; miss the window and the token lapses to a sparrow-level grace state, then dies. Because attention is serial and non-parallelizable, operating N identities costs N×30 minutes of real human time daily, a comet of effort that cannot be batch-farmed. An attacker sustaining 1,000 identities needs 500 human-hours per day, and the shale of idle identities decays fastest in the first hours.
